# /skill:ship does not need a work item — intake brief

## Problem statement

The global agent workflow states that "Tasks require a work-item id", with no
stated exception for the release action, and the ship skill's agent-facing brief
never says otherwise. An agent asked to run `/skill:ship release` can therefore
believe it must first create a work item (or ask the operator to create one) to
track the release, adding needless worklog noise and friction to a routine,
deterministic maintenance action.

## Users

- **Primary:** AI agents operating under the global workflow (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`),
  who invoke `/skill:ship release` and currently cannot tell from the ship brief
  whether a work item is required.
- **Secondary:** human producers/operators, who review a cleaner worklog and stop
  being asked to create release-only work items.

Example user stories:

- As an AI agent about to release, I want the ship skill to state explicitly that
  no work item is required, so that I do not create a spurious release work item
  or block on the "tasks require a work-item id" rule.
- As a producer, I want the release path documented as work-item-exempt, so that
  my worklog contains only real, trackable work.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/ship/SKILL.md` explicitly states that running `/skill:ship release`
   does **not** require a work item and that agents must **not** create one for
   the release; the statement is prominent (in or directly next to "When To Use"
   / "Prerequisites"), not buried in a deep section.
2. The statement distinguishes release-time work-item **closure** (already
   automatic in `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`, Release Process step 12) from
   creating a release work item, so the two are not confused.
3. `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` reflects the same policy consistently (and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` if that is the shipped copy),
   with no contradictory text anywhere in the ship documentation.
4. At least one regression test asserts the explicit "no work item required for a
   release" statement is present in `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, so it cannot be
   silently dropped; the test fails on the pre-change content and passes after.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Documentation-only change: no runtime behaviour of `run-release.js` or any ship
  script changes.
- Write in UK English; follow existing ship-doc conventions.
- Keep the change surgical — do not restructure the ship skill.
- Do not edit `.pi/`, `command/`, or other agent infrastructure beyond the skills
  and docs explicitly in scope. (This repository is the canonical source for
  `skill/`, so editing `skill/ship/` is in scope here.)
- `CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the release pipeline and must not be edited.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` documents "When To Use", "Prerequisites", the release
  process, and the automatic close-work-items step (step 12), but contains no
  statement about whether a work item is required to run a release.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` states "Tasks require a work-item id; if not provided, ask
  for one to be created or get permission to create one", with no release
  exemption; its push-policy note already points at the ship skill.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the skill-local
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` are the maintainer references.
- Existing precedent for content assertions on agent guidance lives in
  `tests/dev/critical.mjs` (e.g. it already asserts ship-skill and
  AGENTS_GLOBAL.md content).

## Desired change

Add an explicit, visible policy note to `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — for example under
"When To Use" or "Prerequisites" — stating that the `release` action is
work-item-exempt: no work item is needed to run a release, agents must not create
one for it, and the existing post-release closure of `in_review` items is a
separate, automatic step. Mirror the policy in the ship reference doc(s) and add
a regression test pinning the statement.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — add the explicit "no work item required for a release"
  policy note near "When To Use"/"Prerequisites".
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — mirror the policy in the maintainer
  reference.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — mirror if this is the shipped
  duplicate of the reference (verify which copy is authoritative before editing).
- `tests/dev/critical.mjs` — add a content-assertion regression test for the
  statement in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (or a new focused test file if a better
  home exists).
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — optionally add a one-line cross-reference that the ship
  release is work-item-exempt, if the implementer judges it necessary to remove
  the blanket "Tasks require a work-item id" ambiguity.

## Related work

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQKYF089003Y85H** – Ensure all skills and commands update work item status and stage on completion (completed)
- **SA-0MS4KVN5E002H0B1** – Refactor ship skill to single 'release' action (completed)
- **SA-0MRGTMMBB003H1QT** – Refactor AGENTS.md, commands, and skill files for conciseness and to remove duplication (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — matched: create, explicit, item, items, make (+6 more)
- `README.md` — matched: create, explicit, item, items, make (+6 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: create, explicit, item, items, make (+6 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the seed context is sufficient; no interview round was needed. Recorded in the Appendix.
- **Assumption:** the policy belongs primarily in `skill/ship/SKILL.md`; the reference docs are secondary. If the producer disagrees, the change relocates without affecting the ACs.
- **Risk — doc drift:** the policy is duplicated across `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and the reference doc(s); mitigate by wording it once and cross-referencing, and by the regression test.
- **Risk — scope creep:** a release-pipeline flag or configuration option (e.g. "allow release work items") would change runtime behaviour; explicitly out of scope — record any such idea as a separate linked work item.
- **Risk — brittle test:** over-specific phrasing assertions could break on harmless rewording; assert on a stable key phrase, not full sentences.
- **Failure mode:** if the note is added in a deep section only, discoverability is poor and the confusion persists; mitigate with the placement requirement in AC1.

## Open Questions / Assumptions

- **Assumption:** the statement belongs primarily in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (the
  agent-facing brief), mirrored in the maintainer reference. The seed context
  ("/skill:ship does not need a work item") is sufficient to proceed without an
  interview round.
- **Open question (non-blocking):** whether to also amend `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`'s
  blanket "Tasks require a work-item id" line with a release exemption, or rely on
  the ship brief alone. Recommendation: ship brief is authoritative; add the
  AGENTS_GLOBAL.md cross-reference only if it can be done in one surgical line.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (title
  "/skill:ship does not need a work item" + description "Make it explicit that
  /skill:ship does not need to create work items for the release process")
  suffices to draft a clear brief. Assumptions are recorded above and flagged as
  non-blocking.

# Enforce and document that driven child sessions must work inside their worktree (cwd is not enough)

## Problem statement

Driven child sessions can write **outside their worktree** — typically into the main checkout — because nothing verifies that the child is *operating in* the worktree directory; `cwd` is only a hint that an agent can override by prefixing commands with `cd <main-checkout> && ...`. When that happens, the work-item's work lands in the main checkout, the isolation model silently breaks, and the parent/`drive` phase cannot advance.

### Incident evidence

Repo `tce-main-street`, epic `MS-0MUXW90YE009L4DQ`. A driven child for `MS-0MUXWGT7G009THBO` was spawned with `cwd` = its worktree. It ran `pwd`/`git status` and saw the worktree branch `wl-MS-0MUXWGT7G009THBO-...`, then:

- prefixed **all 76 `bash` calls** with `cd /home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street && ...` (the main checkout),
- wrote **all 20 `write` + 4 `edit`** files to absolute paths under the main checkout,
- referenced the worktree path **0 times**, and
- never called `implement.py start` / `finish`.

Result: the child's work landed in the main checkout; untracked files there later blocked the next `implement.py start` on the dirty-tree safety gate; `finish` had no worktree changes to commit; and `phase_parent`/`drive` could not advance.

## Users

- **Implement-skill maintainer** — wants a deterministic guard that isolates child work to its worktree.
- **Producer/operator running `/skill:implement <epic>`** — wants an actionable failure naming the offending paths, not a silent stall.
- **Driven child agent** — needs explicit, copy-pasteable guidance on verifying its worktree root and on running `wl` without leaving the worktree.

Example user stories:

- As an implement-skill maintainer, I want driven child sessions to be forced and verified to operate in their own worktree, so that per-child isolation holds and `finish`/`phase_parent` advance correctly.
- As a producer running `/skill:implement <epic>`, I want a clear, actionable failure when a child writes to the main checkout instead of its worktree, rather than a silent pass or an opaque stall.
- As an agent working a child item, I want documentation that states exactly how to confirm I am in the worktree and how to run `wl` against the main checkout's `.worklog` while keeping every edit inside the worktree.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` explicitly requires a child/driven session to verify it is operating in the worktree directory (with a concrete command, e.g. comparing `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` with the expected `wl-<id>-<slug>` path) before its first write, and forbids editing via absolute paths under the main checkout; the requirement is repeated in the session-per-child (Step 6.1) section.
2. `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`'s "MANDATORY — worktree requirement" states that `cwd` is not sufficient, that every write/edit path must resolve inside the worktree, and that a child/driven session must verify its worktree root before its first edit.
3. A guard in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` detects when a driven child produced changes in the main checkout instead of its worktree (child non-terminal **and** main checkout dirty outside `.worklog/` **and** the worktree clean at the parent branch HEAD) and reports an actionable failure naming the offending main-checkout paths; the parent/`drive` phase fails closed instead of silently proceeding.
4. A regression test exercises the guard with a simulated spawned child that wrote to the main checkout and asserts an actionable failure is reported, and that a legitimate in-worktree child is unaffected (**testing/validation criterion**).
5. Documentation explains the `wl`-needs-main-checkout vs edits-need-worktree split, including the correct way to run `wl` from inside a worktree (e.g. `wl --worklog-dir <main-checkout>/.worklog ...`), so agents do not `cd` to the main checkout in order to edit.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scope is limited to this framework repository (canonical `skill/` and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`); no behaviour change to `wl` itself.
- Preserve the existing `_worktree_placement_violation` semantics (the cwd-sensitive `phase_finish` gate) — extend it rather than regress it; existing enforcement tests must continue to pass.
- Any marker file or environment variable introduced must not pollute the repository working tree (a marker must be gitignored, or an env-var/`git rev-parse` check preferred).
- UK English; follow existing skill/command conventions.
- Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md` (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `implement.py`:
  - `_child_session_env()` (~line 4270) only sets the drive recursion guard and clears the parent session identity; it injects **no** worktree information into the child environment.
  - `_default_session_spawner()` (~line 4333) runs `pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve` with `cwd=worktree_path` (~line 4383) — cwd only, no verification.
  - `_worktree_placement_violation()` (~line 4660) already exists and returns an actionable message when work landed in the main checkout, but it is only called from `phase_finish` Step 0.5 (~line 3322) and returns `None` whenever the caller's cwd is inside the worktree. `phase_parent()` / `phase_drive()` do **not** call it.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`: Step 5 has a "MANDATORY — worktree requirement" block (cd-into-worktree); Step 6.1 documents session-per-child worktree isolation — neither requires *verifying* the worktree root.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` line 39: "MANDATORY — worktree requirement" is worded in terms of `cd` into the worktree (cwd-only).
- Existing tests: `tests/test_implement_worktree_enforcement.py` (direct unit tests of `_worktree_placement_violation`), `tests/test_implement_worktree_repo_root.py`, `tests/test_agents_global_session_per_child.py`.

## Desired change

- Add a first-class, verified worktree-root check to `SKILL.md` (Step 5 and Step 6.1) and strengthen `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` so `cwd` is explicitly insufficient.
- Add a defensive guard in `implement.py` so `phase_parent`/`drive` detect a child that produced changes in the main checkout and fail closed with an actionable message.
- Document the `wl`-vs-edits split, including the correct worktree-safe way to run `wl`.
- Add regression tests for the guard and the documentation content.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Add a verified worktree-root check and forbid absolute main-checkout edit paths; repeat in the session-per-child section.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — Strengthen the "MANDATORY — worktree requirement" to state that cwd is not sufficient and that the worktree root must be verified before the first edit.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Inject worktree identity in `_child_session_env()`; optionally write a gitignored worktree marker in `phase_start()`; add child-placement detection to `phase_parent()`/`phase_drive()`, reusing/extending `_worktree_placement_violation()`.
- `tests/test_implement_worktree_enforcement.py` — Regression tests for the new parent/drive guard (actionable failure; in-worktree child unaffected).
- `tests/test_agents_global_session_per_child.py` — Assert the strengthened AGENTS_GLOBAL wording.
- `docs/dev/` (e.g. a worktree/workflow doc) — Document the `wl`-needs-main-checkout vs edits-need-worktree split and the correct `wl` invocation from a worktree.

## Related work

- `SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9` — implement skill: drive all epic children to completion (fresh session per child) (completed) — introduces `phase_drive` and the per-child session spawner central to this issue.
- `SA-0MUCMO5YV008RD83` — Update skill/implement/SKILL.md Step 6.1 — document session-per-child behaviour (completed).
- `SA-0MUCMMYTV008QWI2` — Update AGENTS_GLOBAL.md with session-per-child procedural step (completed).
- `SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM` — Implement skill safety gate should account for git worktrees (completed) — precedent for `_worktree_placement_violation`.
- `SA-0MUUIJIU7006VACQ` — Add concrete skill-session ACs to operational/delivery skills (blocked) — related AC wording conventions.
- `SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2` — Enforce git worktree usage for all implementation work (completed).
- `SA-0MSHQIADG003PBC4` — implement.py finish refuses to remove worktree when run from inside it (completed).
- Incident: repo `tce-main-street`, epic `MS-0MUXW90YE009L4DQ`, child `MS-0MUXWGT7G009THBO`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — guard false positives:** a legitimate child may leave pre-existing/unrelated dirt in the main checkout. Mitigation: require all three conditions (child non-terminal, main dirty outside `.worklog/`, worktree clean at parent HEAD), mirroring the existing `_worktree_placement_violation` precision.
- **Risk — scope creep into a full runtime sandbox:** the guard is detection + actionable failure, not OS-level confinement. Out of scope: preventing writes at the filesystem layer (record as a linked work item if pursued).
- **Risk — marker-file pollution:** a worktree marker committed accidentally. Mitigation: prefer env var + `git rev-parse`; gitignore any marker.
- **Assumption:** the seed context (incident report + proposed changes + ACs) is sufficiently detailed to define the work; no clarifying interview was required.
- **Assumption:** the `wl` worktree-safe invocation is `wl --worklog-dir <main-checkout>/.worklog ...` (the mechanism already used by skills); confirmed during implementation and documented.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked: the seed context (an incident report with the exact failure sequence, a list of proposed changes, and four acceptance criteria) already defines the problem, users, scope, constraints, and measurable outcomes.

Recorded assumptions instead of questions:

- **Scope** — the fix includes documentation *and* a defensive `implement.py` guard plus regression tests, as proposed in the seed context.
- **Guard semantics** — fail-closed (actionable error, child not silently advanced), consistent with AC "reports an actionable failure (not a silent pass)".
- **`wl` invocation** — document `wl --worklog-dir <main-checkout>/.worklog ...` from the worktree as the supported way to keep edits worktree-local.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS0DK6BD001RNDG** – implement.py abort script deletes entire project directory when aborting from main working tree (completed)
- **SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E** – [CRITICAL] Audit runner has circular dependency — child audit verdict blocks parent regardless of stage (completed)
- **SA-0MPDZE6LZ008WKR3** – Implement: Release manager merge workflow (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absolute, acceptance, acs, actionable, add (+304 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absolute, acceptance, acs, actionable, add (+279 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0muwnhkqh0034dw9, absolute, accidentally, actionable, add (+252 more)
